title: Retreat Dribble and Re-Attack
description: Ball handlers learn to back out of pressure with a retreat dribble, keeping their eyes up, then re-attack the gap or reset the offense.

content.objective: Escape a trap or a cut-off with a backward retreat dribble, keep the ball alive and re-attack before the defense recovers.
content.setup: A ball handler starts at the wing; a defender stands in front at arm's length. A second line waits at the top.
content.organization: Partners rotate: offense to defense, defense to the back of the line.
instructions: The ball handler attacks the defender toward the baseline.
The defender cuts off the drive; the ball handler takes two retreat dribbles straight back, body sideways, ball on the far hip.
As the defender closes, the ball handler crosses or changes pace and re-attacks the middle.
Play 1v1 live to a finish or a stop.
coachingPoints: Retreat with the shoulders turned so the body protects the ball.
Keep the eyes on the rim, not the defender's hands.
Re-attack the moment the defender's weight goes forward.
commonMistakes: Turning the back completely and losing sight of the floor.
Picking up the dribble while backing up.
Retreating too far and stalling the offense.
content.safety: Defenders play the ball, not the body; no reaching across the face.
progressions: Add a second defender to create a trap.
Re-attack must end in a pass to a cutter.
regressions: Defender is passive and only shows the cut-off.
Retreat without a defender, on the coach's whistle.
variations: Start at the top against a hedging defender.
Limit the re-attack to three dribbles.
successCriteria: Keeps the dribble alive through the retreat every time.
Re-attacks within two dribbles of the retreat.
content.gameApplication: Retreat dribbles get ball handlers out of traps and corners, where most turnovers happen.
